title: Monoidal categories and tensor notation
statement:
A monoidal category is a category $\mathcal C$ [def-nagata-category] equipped with a bifunctor $\otimes:\mathcal C\times\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$, a specified object $\mathbf1$, and natural isomorphisms
$\alpha_{X,Y,Z}:(X\otimes Y)\otimes Z\xrightarrow{\sim}X\otimes(Y\otimes Z)$,
$\lambda_X:\mathbf1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ and $\rho_X:X\otimes\mathbf1\xrightarrow{\sim}X$.
For all objects $W,X,Y,Z$ the pentagon identity is
$$
(\mathrm{id}_W\otimes\alpha_{X,Y,Z})\circ\alpha_{W,X\otimes Y,Z}\circ(\alpha_{W,X,Y}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Z)
=\alpha_{W,X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{W\otimes X,Y,Z},
$$
and the triangle identity is
$$
(\mathrm{id}_X\otimes\lambda_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,\mathbf1,Y}
=\rho_X\otimes\mathrm{id}_Y.
$$
Here $f\otimes g$ denotes the image of the pair of morphisms $(f,g)$ under the tensor bifunctor, and composition $b\circ a$ means first $a$, then $b$.
An isomorphism is a morphism with a specified two-sided inverse; naturality means that these structural isomorphisms commute with the morphisms induced by the tensor bifunctor.
Here a bifunctor assigns an object to each pair of objects and a morphism to each pair of morphisms, preserving identities and componentwise composition.
